articles.headline: RHSA‑2026:51746 rolls out kernel security, bug‑fix and enhancement update for RHEL
articles.dek: Red Hat’s latest kernel update patches critical CVEs, fixes stability bugs, and adds low‑overhead enhancements that matter for AI workloads on the cloud.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Red Hat Enterprise Linux now ships a new kernel (RHSA‑2026:51746) that patches high‑severity vulnerabilities and smooths out bugs that can interrupt AI training jobs; apply it now to keep your Cloud‑Native stacks safe and stable. [FACT:c28361c275aaa71bfc14621804905e9d][FACT:734a4f8cff38efedf57e56bbee054287]
Why This Matters

AI pipelines depend on a stable OS kernel—any slip can corrupt model checkpoints or cause node‑level crashes. The update’s CVSS‑rated fixes target the same attack surface that threat‑actors exploit in multi‑tenant clouds, so skipping it raises real exposure. [FACT:9dc4790ffefdc6a4d40361c936424e5b][FACT:734a4f8cff38efedf57e56bbee054287]
What Happened

Red Hat published the advisory on 7 August 2026, marking the kernel as “important” in the product‑security rating. The bundle includes patches for several CVEs, each assigned a CVSS base score that reflects a medium‑to‑high severity, plus non‑security bug fixes and performance‑tuned enhancements. [FACT:c28361c275aaa71bfc14621804905e9d][FACT:734a4f8cff38efedf57e56bbee054287][FACT:9dc4790ffefdc6a4d40361c936424e5b]
Builder View

If you run AI workloads on RHEL‑based VMs or containers, schedule the update before the next training window. The patches won’t break existing drivers, but they do tighten seccomp filters that some custom kernels relied on—test a copy of the image first. This is a “apply‑and‑verify” move, not a “skip‑and‑hope‑for‑the‑best.” [FACT:c28361c275aaa71bfc14621804905e9d]
Open Questions

Red Hat has not published performance benchmarks for the new kernel under heavy tensor workloads, so the exact latency impact remains unknown. Also, the rollout timeline for default cloud images (e.g., AWS RHEL 9) is still pending. Keep an eye on the Red Hat portal for rollout notices. [FACT:734a4f8cff38efedf57e56bbee054287]
Ardur Take

Two independent Red Hat advisories corroborate the same security rating and CVSS data, giving this update a high confidence level. Builders should treat it as a mandatory patch for any production AI stack and verify compatibility in a staging environment before full rollout. [FACT:c28361c275aaa71bfc14621804905e9d][FACT:734a4f8cff38efedf57e56bbee054287]

keyPoints: RHSA‑2026:51746 delivers kernel patches for high‑severity CVEs affecting RHEL.
The update also fixes stability bugs that can interrupt AI training jobs.
Low‑overhead performance tweaks accompany the security fixes.
Apply the update before your next cloud training window; test in staging first.
articles.whyItMatters: AI workloads run at scale on RHEL; an unpatched kernel can become the weakest link in your cloud‑security chain, potentially exposing data and crashing training jobs.
articles.readerAction: Pull the latest kernel package from Red Hat’s repository (yum update kernel) and run your CI validation suite before promoting the change to production.

articles.headline: Metabase SQLi zero‑day exploited in customer data‑theft attacks
articles.dek: An unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Metabase is being weaponised in the wild; cloud customers have been forced onto a patched release.

body.text: Key Takeaway

Metabase confirmed that a critical unauthenticated SQL injection zero‑day (CVE‑2026‑XXXX) is actively being used to steal customer data. The vendor blocked the abused endpoints and pushed an emergency patch to all cloud users. Builders must verify they run the patched version or stay exposed. [FACT:4c27e8035c0f79c84b349a518d6609ed][FACT:2c0f2798fc7806680db2d01d2ebdb84a][FACT:af425877fb5604e4bde62b36848fab84][FACT:452f2f2868dcce8163c1130778888b61]
Why This Matters

The flaw lets any remote attacker run arbitrary queries without credentials, opening the door to wholesale data exfiltration from analytics dashboards that sit behind your AI pipelines. In cloud‑hosted Metabase this translates to a direct path from a public endpoint to your raw data stores. [FACT:b5a0ccd44fdac5a34757791e01acba82][FACT:64f6fb776e3ba6beed5dde83324f6e9f]
What Happened

Metabase’s security team detected suspicious activity on its cloud platform and disclosed the issue on Thursday. Since then, they have observed active exploitation targeting multiple tenants. The attack chain leverages the unauthenticated SQL injection to pull exported query results and dump them elsewhere. [FACT:4c27e8035c0f79c84b349a518d6609ed][FACT:2c0f2798fc7806680db2d01d2ebdb84a][FACT:27524f37b7f44df6f36488cbcacde678][FACT:955094f5e454772a4c8ddba214b8b589]
Builder View

First step: check the version string in your Metabase instance; any release after the emergency patch (v0.49.5‑security‑fix) is safe. Next, audit your network logs for outbound calls from the now‑blocked /api/sql endpoint. Finally, enable MFA on any service that consumes Metabase‑exported CSVs or JSONs to cut off a secondary exfiltration channel. [FACT:af425877fb5604e4bde62b36848fab84][FACT:452f2f2868dcce8163c1130778888b61][FACT:64f6fb776e3ba6beed5dde83324f6e9f]
Open Questions
Active exploitation is confirmed, and the community is still mapping the full range of affected query patterns and detection signatures. [FACT:27524f37b7f44df6f36488cbcacde678]
Ardur Take

The only public disclosure comes from a single security outlet, but the vendor’s own statements and the observed cloud attacks give us medium confidence that the vulnerability is real and being weaponised. Upgrade now and monitor for any residual SQL‑endpoint traffic. [FACT:4c27e8035c0f79c84b349a518d6609ed][FACT:2c0f2798fc7806680db2d01d2ebdb84a][FACT:af425877fb5604e4bde62b36848fab84]

keyPoints: Metabase’s unauthenticated SQL injection zero‑day is being used in active data‑theft campaigns. [FACT:4c27e8035c0f79c84b349a518d6609ed]
The vendor blocked the compromised endpoints and released an emergency patch for all cloud customers. [FACT:af425877fb5604e4bde62b36848fab84][FACT:452f2f2868dcce8163c1130778888b61]
Builders must confirm they run the patched version and scrub logs for any calls to the now‑blocked /api/sql path. [FACT:af425877fb5604e4bde62b36848fab84]
articles.whyItMatters: Unauthenticated remote code execution against a data‑visualisation layer gives attackers inexpensive access to the raw datasets that power AI models, making this a high‑impact risk for any cloud‑native analytics stack. [FACT:b5a0ccd44fdac5a34757791e01acba82][FACT:64f6fb776e3ba6beed5dde83324f6e9f]
articles.readerAction: Log into your Metabase admin console, verify the version is the post‑patch release, and scan your network for any traffic to /api/sql. If you’re on a self‑hosted deployment, apply the patch manually and rotate any credentials that may have been exposed.
